blocks.content: Submergent coasts are formed due to the subsidence of land or a rise in sea level, whereas emergent coasts result from tectonic uplift or a fall in sea level.

rows: Land uplift or relative drop in sea level
Land subsidence or relative rise in sea level
Raised beaches, wave-cut platforms, sea caves
Ria coasts, Fjord coasts, Estuaries, Lagoons (Kayals)
Less suitable for natural harbors; requires dredging
Highly suitable for natural deep-water ports

items: Frequently asked: Match the coast type to Indian geography (Konkan Coast = Submergent, Coromandel Coast = Emergent).
Identify landforms: Rias and Fjords belong strictly to submergent coasts, while wave-cut benches belong to emergent coasts.
Port suitability: Submergent coastlines provide natural deep-water harbors due to their indented nature, unlike emergent coastlines.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Emergent coasts are formed by tectonic uplift of the land or a fall in sea level.
Submergent coasts occur due to land subsidence or a relative rise in global sea levels.
Rias, Fjords, estuaries, and drowned river valleys are signature landforms of submergent coasts.
Raised beaches, sea cliffs, spit bars, and wave-cut platforms characterize emergent coastlines.
The Western coast of India (Konkan) shows features of submergence, whereas the Eastern coast is largely an emergent coast.
